plain_meaning: Shows the 3-month average of blood sugar levels. Helps see long-term sugar trends rather than just day-to-day fluctuations.
lifestyle_action: Brisk 30-minute evening walk after dinner, avoiding prolonged sitting, and having meals at consistent times.
indian_food_swaps: Replace polished white rice with whole wheat chapatis or fiber-rich jowar and bajra rotis
Drink methi dana (fenugreek) water soaked overnight on an empty stomach in the morning
Snack on dry roasted bhuna chana or boiled sprouts instead of maida biscuits and rusks
Include steamed moong dal chilla with mint-coriander chutney instead of white bread toast
Enjoy bitter gourd (karela) sabzi or bottle gourd (lauki) soup twice a week

plain_meaning: Reflects your baseline blood glucose after 8-10 hours of overnight fasting.
lifestyle_action: Ensure at least 7 hours of sound sleep and finish dinner 2.5 hours before sleeping.
indian_food_swaps: Have cinnamon (dalchini) infused warm water in the morning
Swap sugary morning chai with ginger-tulsi herbal tea with no added sugar
Switch morning poha/upma to vegetable dalia (broken wheat) with green beans and carrots
Keep evening snacks limited to roasted makhana (fox nuts) roasted with light turmeric and salt
Add fresh homemade curd (dahi) with ground roasted jeera powder to your lunch

plain_meaning: Total amount of fat circulating in the blood. Sparing use of deep-frying keeps this comfortably balanced.
lifestyle_action: 30-40 minutes of daily aerobic movement like brisk walking, yoga, or cycling.
indian_food_swaps: Replace deep-fried samosas and pakoras with air-fried or roasted chana and steamed dhokla
Cook sabzis in cold-pressed mustard oil or sesame/groundnut oil, strictly limiting to 2-3 teaspoons per person daily
Drink garlic-infused warm water or chew 1 clove of raw crushed garlic on an empty stomach
Incorporate isabgol (psyllium husk) in warm water at bedtime to aid cholesterol binding
Add soluble fiber through daily servings of seasonal sabzi like tori (ridge gourd) and bhindi

plain_meaning: Circulating blood fats derived directly from excess carbohydrates, refined sugars, and oils.
lifestyle_action: Avoid late-night snacks, cut sweetened drinks, and practice brisk walking after major meals.
indian_food_swaps: Eliminate sweets like mithai, halwa, gulab jamun, and sweetened lassi
Swap evening white bread and namkeen with roasted chana and flaxseed (alsi) powder
Replace refined sunflower oils and vanaspati ghee with minimal mustard or groundnut oil
Add raw amla (Indian gooseberry) juice or fresh amla chutney to your midday plate
Choose unsweetened buttermilk (chaas) infused with curry leaves and hing over cold drinks

plain_meaning: The protective 'good cholesterol' that carries excess fats away from arteries back to the liver.
lifestyle_action: Consistent daily physical exercise and brisk walking are proven to raise protective HDL naturally.
indian_food_swaps: Take 1 teaspoon of roasted alsi (flaxseeds) and pumpkin seeds daily with water
Eat 4-5 soaked almonds (badam) and 1 whole walnut (akhrot) every morning
Include cooked rajma, chana, or lobia (black-eyed peas) for healthy legumes and minerals
Use fresh curry leaves (kadi patta) generously in tadka for natural antioxidant polyphenols
Drink freshly prepared warm lemon water with a pinch of black salt

plain_meaning: Often called 'bad cholesterol'. Keeping this low prevents plaque buildup inside blood vessels.
lifestyle_action: Avoid commercial bakery biscuits, palm oil snacks, and maintain a 45-minute active routine.
indian_food_swaps: Replace butter-laden parathas with plain phulkas dry-roasted without surface vanaspati
Include fiber-dense ragi (finger millet) rotis or oats porridge with cardamom and milk
Snack on fresh papaya, guava, or pomegranate instead of fried namkeen or bhujia
Drink warm water with 1 teaspoon methi powder before lunch
Have steamed moong dal with turmeric and cumin seeds for lunch and dinner

plain_meaning: A pituitary signal that controls your thyroid gland. When elevated, it gently nudges the thyroid to speed up energy regulation.
lifestyle_action: Manage stress with Pranayama (Anulom Vilom) and maintain regular sleep cycles.
indian_food_swaps: Drink coriander seed (dhaniya dana) soaked water boiled and cooled every morning
Eat 1-2 Brazil nuts or soaked almonds and a pinch of iodized rock salt in cooking
Avoid raw goitrogens like raw cabbage and raw cauliflower; always cook or steam them thoroughly
Include fresh roasted makhana and pumpkin seeds for natural zinc and selenium
Drink warm milk with a pinch of organic turmeric (haldi) at bedtime

plain_meaning: The protein inside red blood cells carrying oxygen throughout the body. Healthy levels sustain vitality and energy.
lifestyle_action: Avoid drinking chai or coffee immediately with meals, as tannins hinder dietary iron absorption.
indian_food_swaps: Eat 2-3 dates (khajoor) and black raisins (kishmish) soaked overnight every morning
Include iron-rich green leafy vegetables like palak (spinach), methi, and bathua saag
Snack on homemade jaggery (gud) and roasted groundnut/chana chikki in moderate quantities
Add fresh beetroot and carrot salad with squeezed lemon juice (Vitamin C enhances iron uptake)
Cook vegetables and dals in traditional cast-iron kadhais to naturally infuse trace iron

plain_meaning: The sunshine vitamin essential for calcium absorption, bone strength, and optimal immunity.
lifestyle_action: Spend 20-30 minutes in early morning sunshine (8:00 AM - 9:30 AM) with bare arms and face.
indian_food_swaps: Consume cow's milk or fortified milk boiled with a pinch of nutmeg (jaiphal)
Include fresh country mushrooms exposed to brief sunlight before cooking
Eat homemade fresh paneer (cottage cheese) lightly tossed with jeera and black pepper
Have set curd (dahi) or fortified dairy products during daytime meals
Include egg yolks or consult your doctor regarding a weekly clinical cholecalciferol sachet

plain_meaning: Vital vitamin for nerve health, brain vitality, and healthy red blood cell synthesis.
lifestyle_action: Maintain good gut digestion through probiotics to optimize digestive absorption.
indian_food_swaps: Drink a glass of warm milk boiled with cardamom twice daily
Have fresh homemade set curd (dahi) or spiced chaas with roasted cumin daily
Include fresh paneer or fortified nutritional yeast in daily vegetarian cooking
For non-vegetarians, include boiled eggs or light country chicken stew once or twice a week
Consult your physician regarding sublingual methylcobalamin if following a strict vegan diet

plain_meaning: A byproduct of purine breakdown in foods. When elevated, drinking ample water helps flush it through kidneys.
lifestyle_action: Hydrate generously with 2.5 to 3 liters of clean water daily to assist renal clearance.
indian_food_swaps: Drink freshly prepared coconut water (nariyal pani) or barley (jau) water
Limit heavy high-purine dals like rajma and chole; favor light split moong dal
Eliminate sugary sodas and packaged fruit beverages high in industrial fructose syrup
Include fresh cherries, amla, and cucumber salad with lemon dressing
Drink warm water with 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar or lemon juice before meals

plain_meaning: A natural muscle breakdown waste product cleanly filtered by healthy kidneys. Indicates filtration efficiency.
lifestyle_action: Keep blood pressure and hydration strictly monitored, avoiding unprescribed painkiller NSAID tablets.
indian_food_swaps: Hydrate with warm water and fresh coriander-infused water throughout the daytime
Avoid excess protein powders or heavy unmonitored supplements; stick to natural home-cooked dals
Choose low-potassium vegetables like lauki (bottle gourd), tinda, and parwal cooked lightly
Avoid heavy table salt; use measured rock salt (sendha namak) without excess sprinkling
Drink barley water (jau ka pani) cooked with a hint of roasted cumin

plain_meaning: A liver enzyme that enters the bloodstream during periods of metabolic stress, fatty liver, or heavy meals.
lifestyle_action: Prioritize 45 minutes of brisk walking to reduce hepatic fat accumulation and avoid alcohol completely.
indian_food_swaps: Drink warm water with fresh lemon and a teaspoon of ginger juice every morning
Eat light home-cooked food; avoid street snacks fried in repeatedly heated oil
Include fresh raw turmeric (kacchi haldi) and garlic in your everyday dal tadka
Drink freshly squeezed radish (mooli) leaf juice or amla juice in moderation
Substitute heavy evening meals with khichdi made of yellow moong dal and bottle gourd

plain_meaning: An enzyme found in liver and heart cells. Mild elevations often point to metabolic overload or lack of exercise.
lifestyle_action: Maintain healthy body weight through low-glycemic home food and regular evening exercise.
indian_food_swaps: Sip warm green tea or jeera-ajwain boiled digestive water after lunch and dinner
Eliminate bakery puff pastries, samosas, and commercial sweets
Consume boiled or lightly sauteed seasonal vegetables like tori, lauki, and methi saag
Take 1 teaspoon crushed amla powder with warm water
Snack on sliced cucumbers, carrots, and roasted makhana instead of biscuits

plain_meaning: Crucial blood cell fragments responsible for normal blood clotting and tissue repair after injury.
lifestyle_action: Rest adequately, avoid strenuous contact sports during low counts, and maintain steady hydration.
indian_food_swaps: Consume fresh papaya leaf extract or chew tender fresh papaya leaf juice (1-2 teaspoons)
Drink fresh kiwi fruit pulp or eat 1-2 fresh ripe kiwis daily
Eat fresh pomegranate (anar) pearls or drink fresh pomegranate juice without added sugar
Include tender coconut water twice daily for electrolyte balance and cellular hydration
Drink giloy (Tinospora cordifolia) extract or boiled giloy water under guidance
